markers.reading: Opening: Wellby and Delwath wait in the dining hall in late afternoon, about three hours before sunset.

evidence.quote: DM: So, for the moment, all is quiet in the late afternoon sun at the Monastery of Bhishma. About three hours before sunset. Wellby and Delwath are sitting in the middle of the main dining hall, waiting for Seeker and Kenzo to return from their journey deeper into the mysteries of the Monastery of Bhishma. About an hour ago, this was the lair of a manticore family. The bodies of the four dead manticores—two adults and two young—lie where you killed them, the foul smell of their blood beginning to drift through the large room in the still air. Outside, the distant banging of the sole survivor of the battle, left locked in the bath house, has faded. Because dead companions lying with the—[garbled].

evidence.quote: DM: So, so—I'm—all of you remember this story that Seeker told once of his dead brother, and for a minute you are there, standing, you know, on the, on the, on the, on the mountain side. A small, lizard-like winged creature, scales a faded purple trending to pale white, like a threadbare purple robe stretched thin over frosted glass—I'm—flies out of the shadow towards you—I'm—pacing slowly back and forth. You kneel, see a glimpse in the shadows of something green, and a voice begins to crack, echo out a little bit, um, but the words don't mean anything to you. You don't understand the words. DM: You—so, so, as you, as you reach—as you hold this kind of thought and reach out for this memory, um, you feel something outside the memories reaching as well. I know, I know that is not what we are taught. That is not how an army should behave. But fighting on the edge of Drankor now seems like a terrible idea. We should be protecting the borders.
